title: “ready to die” (Revelation 3:2) — Tischendorf’s Greek has a past-tense verb
summary: KJV Revelation 3:2 has Sardis strengthen “the things which remain, that are ready to die”. The Textus Receptus text served prints present μέλλει; Tischendorf’s text prints imperfect ἔμελλον, “were about to die”.
text: KJV Revelation 3:2: “Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 3:2: γίνου γρηγορῶν, καὶ στήρισον τὰ λοιπὰ ἃ ἔμελλον ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ γὰρ εὕρηκά σου τὰ ἔργα πεπληρωμένα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ μου· Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) Revelation 3:2: ... α μελλει αποθανειν ου γαρ ευρηκα σου τα εργα πεπληρωμενα ενωπιον του θεου Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/3/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/3/.
reasoning: The KJV “are ready to die” follows present μέλλει. Tischendorf’s ἔμελλον puts the dying in the past (“were about to die”), a small shift from a present danger to one already near. Tischendorf’s verse also ends “my God” (τοῦ θεοῦ μου), where the TR text served ends “God”.
scope: T applies at Revelation 3:2 only. The difference is between Greek editions: the Textus Receptus text served agrees with the KJV here and Tischendorf’s text does not. This record does not say which reading is original, and two digital editions are not a survey of manuscripts. Only the verb is compared here; the closing “my God” is noted in the reasoning, not claimed as a separate record. title: “no man shutteth” (Revelation 3:7) — Tischendorf’s Greek has future verbs
summary: KJV Revelation 3:7 has Christ “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth”. The Textus Receptus text served prints present κλείει and ἀνοίγει; Tischendorf’s text prints future κλείσει and ἀνοίξει, and the key is τὴν κλεῖν Δαυείδ against τὴν κλεῖδα τοῦ Δαβίδ.
text: KJV Revelation 3:7: “And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 3:7: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Φιλαδελφίᾳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· τάδε λέγει ὁ ἅγιος ὁ ἀληθινός, ὁ ἔχων τὴν κλεῖν Δαυείδ, ὁ ἀνοίγων καὶ οὐδεὶς κλείσει, καὶ κλείων καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀνοίξει· Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) Revelation 3:7: ... ο εχων την κλειδα του δαβιδ ο ανοιγων και ουδεις κλειει και κλειει και ουδεις ανοιγει Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/3/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/3/.
reasoning: The KJV follows the present tense: no one shuts what he opens. Tischendorf has the future for the second clause of each pair, “no one will shut … no one will open”, with a present participle for the shutting. The two readings give the same picture of Christ’s sole authority; the tense changes whether the statement is stated as general fact or as what will hold. The spelling of the key and of David is a form difference only.
scope: T applies at Revelation 3:7 only. The difference is between Greek editions: the Textus Receptus text served agrees with the KJV here and Tischendorf’s text does not. This record does not say which reading is original, and two digital editions are not a survey of manuscripts. Only the verb tenses are claimed; the differences in the form of the word for key and of David’s name are spelling. title: “only those men” (Revelation 9:4) — Tischendorf’s Greek has no “only”
summary: KJV Revelation 9:4 limits the locusts to “only those men which have not the seal of God”. The Textus Receptus text served prints μόνους (“only”); Tischendorf’s text omits the word.
text: KJV Revelation 9:4: “And it was commanded them that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree; but only those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 9:4: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον, εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσιν τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων. Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) Revelation 9:4: ... ει μη τους ανθρωπους μονους οιτινες ουκ εχουσιν την σφραγιδα του θεου επι των μετωπων αυτων Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/9/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/9/.
reasoning: In the TR text the exception is stated with “only”; without μόνους, Tischendorf’s “except the men who do not have the seal” still excludes the sealed from harm, so the sense is close, though the KJV’s emphasis is lighter in the shorter text. Tischendorf also lacks the closing “their” (αὐτῶν).

title: “reached unto heaven” (Revelation 18:5) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “were joined” or “piled up”
summary: KJV Revelation 18:5 says Babylon’s “sins have reached unto heaven”. The Textus Receptus text served prints ἠκολούθησαν (“followed”); Tischendorf’s text prints ἐκολλήθησαν (“were joined”, “clung”), the verb behind a sense of sins heaped up to the sky.
text: KJV Revelation 18:5: “For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 18:5: ὅτι ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐμνημόνευσεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ἀδικήματα αὐτῆς. Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) Revelation 18:5: οτι ηκολουθησαν αυτης αι αμαρτιαι αχρι του ουρανου και εμνημονευσεν ο θεος τα αδικηματα αυτης Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/18/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/18/.
reasoning: The KJV “reached” is a free rendering of either verb. The TR verb literally means “followed” and Tischendorf’s means “were glued, joined together”, so the two editions differ in a single verb with a different picture: sins following her to heaven, or sins stuck together in a pile reaching it.
